chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:
The Talbiyah of the Mu'tamir is cut off when he enters the Haram.

key_terms.الْحَرَمَ: Al-Haram: The sacred precincts of Mecca.
key_terms.تَلْبِيَةُ: Talbiyah: The ritual invocation 'Labbayk Allahumma labbayk' recited by pilgrims.

ai.seo_question: When does the Mu'tamir stop reciting the Talbiyah during Umrah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the legal ruling that the pilgrim performing Umrah must cease reciting the Talbiyah upon entering the sacred boundary of the Haram. In Shia jurisprudence, this marks the transition from the state of Ihram preparation to the actual performance of the Umrah rites, distinguishing it from the continuous recitation in Hajj. The chain of transmission highlights the reliability of the Imams' teachings through key narrators like Zurarah and Aban ibn Taghlib.
